title: The Necklace: theme, inference and word meaning
prompt: Read the excerpt, then choose the best answer for each question.

items.stem: When the necklace is returned, Madame Forestier speaks "with a chilly manner." What does "chilly" mean here?

choices.text: Cold from the weather
choices.misconception: reads "chilly" as the temperature rather than her manner

choices.text: Nervous and shaky
choices.misconception: misses the scolding in "You should have returned it sooner"

choices.text: Cool and unfriendly
Warm and grateful
choices.misconception: ignores the word's negative connotation and her complaint about the delay

items.stem: The narrator asks, "If she had detected the substitution... Would she not have taken Madame Loisel for a thief?" What can you infer from this?

choices.text: Madame Forestier had accused her of theft before
choices.misconception: infers a past accusation the text never mentions

choices.text: Madame Loisel hid the loss partly from fear of being judged dishonest
Madame Loisel really did steal the necklace
choices.misconception: overlooks that she lost it and bought a replacement

choices.text: Madame Forestier opened the case and grew suspicious
choices.misconception: contradicts "She did not open the case"

items.stem: Which statement best expresses a theme of the excerpt?

choices.text: The story is about jewelry
choices.misconception: gives a topic instead of a statement about life

choices.text: Hiding a mistake instead of admitting it can cost far more than the truth would have
Madame Loisel loses a necklace and works for ten years to replace it
choices.misconception: retells the plot instead of stating a theme

choices.text: Rich people are always cruel to the poor
choices.misconception: states a theme the text contradicts: Madame Forestier is "deeply moved"

items.stem: After ten years, Madame Loisel has become "strong and hard and rough." In this sentence, "hard" means

choices.text: solid like stone
choices.misconception: takes the everyday meaning of "hard", not its meaning for a person

choices.text: cruel to other people
choices.misconception: reads "hard" as cruel, though the text describes only her labor

choices.text: toughened by work and hardship
difficult to understand
choices.misconception: reads "hard" as "difficult", which doesn't fit a description of her

items.stem: Taking the whole excerpt together, what can you infer about how poverty changed Madame Loisel?

choices.text: It made her bitter toward everyone
choices.misconception: overlooks her "sudden heroism" and her joy at the end

choices.text: It made her tougher and plainer, yet she still longs for the night she was admired
It changed her clothes but not her looks
choices.misconception: contradicts "looked old now" and her "red hands"

choices.text: It made her forget the ball entirely
choices.misconception: contradicts that she "thought of that gay evening"

items.stem: How does the description of Madame Loisel's ten years of labor develop the story's theme?

choices.text: It shows the huge, lasting cost of one lost necklace, which makes the ending bitter
It shows that hard work made her happier and more beautiful
choices.misconception: misreads the development: she now "looked old" and "hard and rough"

choices.text: It is background that has nothing to do with the theme
choices.misconception: misses how the years of labor build the theme toward the ending

choices.text: It shows that Madame Forestier caused her suffering
choices.misconception: takes Mathilde's "because of you!" as the story's theme

items.stem: The Loisels "rented a garret under the roof." What is a "garret"?

choices.text: a small room just under the roof
a garden behind the house
choices.misconception: guesses from the sound of the word, ignoring "under the roof"

choices.text: a servant
choices.misconception: takes the meaning from "dismissed their servant" just before

choices.text: a shop where they sold goods
choices.misconception: ignores the clue that they moved their lodgings there

items.stem: The narrator asks, "What would have happened if she had not lost that necklace?" and adds, "How small a thing is needed to make or ruin us!" Which theme do these lines develop?

choices.text: Life never changes, no matter what happens
choices.misconception: reverses the narrator's "How strange and changeful is life!"

choices.text: Friends should never lend each other jewelry
choices.misconception: turns one plot event into a narrow rule, not a theme

choices.text: A single small event can change the course of a whole life
People should save money for emergencies
choices.misconception: states a general lesson the passage never develops

items.stem: Telling her friend the truth, Madame Loisel "smiled with a joy that was at once proud and ingenuous." What can you infer at that moment?

choices.text: She knew all along that the necklace was fake
choices.misconception: overlooks that the paste is revealed only after her smile

choices.text: She is trying to make her friend feel guilty
choices.misconception: infers a motive the text doesn't support; she is "very glad"

choices.text: She regrets telling the truth
choices.misconception: contradicts her "joy" and "I am very glad"

choices.text: She is proud of repaying the debt and does not suspect her sacrifice was needless

items.stem: Which is the best objective summary of the excerpt?

choices.text: Foolish Madame Loisel ruins her life over a necklace and gets what she deserves.
choices.misconception: adds a personal judgment, so the summary is not objective

choices.text: Madame Loisel meets Madame Forestier in the Champs Elysees and learns the necklace was paste.
choices.misconception: gives only the ending and leaves out the ten years of debt

choices.text: Madame Forestier demands payment, so the Loisels work for ten years.
choices.misconception: adds an event, a demand for payment, that the text lacks

choices.text: After secretly replacing a lost necklace, the Loisels spend ten years paying for it; then Madame Loisel learns the original was fake.
